sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: A list of the currently known Easter eggs and References in Escape from Tarkov.

sections.heading: Factory
sections.text:
| Description |
| Burning barrel on the 1st floor in the offices. A reference to Ray Bradbury's Fahrenheit 451. This is also a quest location for the quest Is This a Reference? by Fence. |
| A crowbar and multicolored valves in the basement. Next to the cistern containers in the dungeon. This is a reference to the Valve company and the never-released Half-Life 3 game. This is also a quest location for the quest Is This a Reference? by Fence. |
| Olenka's poster on the electrical panel. In the room next to the "Gate №0" exit - a reference to both the Olenka chocolate bar, which is in Tarkov and which in turn is a reference to the real-life Alenka chocolate bar, and to the Terminator. This is also a quest location for the quest Is This a Reference? by Fence. |
| The room of the conspiracy and mail lover - there are 2 references in the room: the first is stickers and diagrams on the wall, a reference to the TV series "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia". The second is three doors on the floor, a reference to a YouTuber with the nickname TARKIN, in video the character opens the door to this room, there are many doors and they fall to the floor like dominoes. This is also a quest location for the quest Is This a Reference? by Fence. |
| The blood stain on the column under the numbers 9 3/4, near gate #2, is a reference to Harry Potter. This is also a quest location for the quest Is This a Reference? by Fence. |
| Graffiti on the second floor of the laboratories, in the second room, on the wall - a reference to the game Minesweeper. This is also a quest location for the quest Is This a Reference? by Fence. |
| The staircase presented to the place where the word "Heaven" is written on the ceiling. The exit "Gate No. 3", the staircase next to the trash can is a reference to the song "Stairway to Heaven" by the English rock band Led Zeppelin. This is also a quest location for the quest Is This a Reference? by Fence. |
| Next to the exit "Gate 0", in the corridor, in the broken ceiling you can see a large blue tank with the inscription "Bring the FLUGEGEHEIMEN" is a reference to the film "EuroTrip" (2004) |

sections.heading: Customs
sections.text:
| Description | Screenshot |
| If you go inside of the three-story dormitory and up to the second story of it, there is some graffiti written above the archway into the kitchen which says "Sorry Mario, the princess is in another castle". This reference refers to all fights with the antagonist Bowser before the final world, where the character Toad exclaims, "Thank You Mario, But Our Princess is in Another Castle". | |
| Located in room 212 of the three-story dormitory, there is an idle computer which shows an error message for the Unity Editor, which claims that it has stopped working. This is in reference to the issues faced when working with the engine that Escape From Tarkov is built on. This is also a quest location for the quest Is This a Reference? by Fence. | |
| Within the three-story dormitory, graffiti in the form of the words "Metalika", "Ramstain" and "Limpin Kar" can be seen scribbled on the ceiling. This is a reference to the musical groups "Metallica", "Rammstein" and "Linkin Park". | |
| Inside the center construction yard there is a yellow hardhat on one of the concrete pillars. The japanese text on it translates to "Majima Kensetsu" which means "Majima Construction". This is a reference to the popular Yakuza video game series where Goro Majima runs his own construction company with that name. | |
| Previously, a featuring the BSG's lead animator, Alexander "Kiba" Kovalchuk, was located on the building near the UN checkpoint. After the Customs location was reworked in patch 0.16.0.0.34447 on December 26, 2024, this billboard was removed, but graffiti was added to the wall reading "KIBA was here" (ru: Здесь был КИБА) | |
| At the extraction point "Old Road Gate" there is a toilet seat. | N/A |
| The inscription "не покупай меч" found on a wall near the main bridge translates to "Don't buy sword". This easter egg is linked to the RPG "Candy Box" in which buying a sword starts the quests. |
| Some fuel tanks sports the inscription "Wassup" and a linked website. This is the short form for "What's up" and refer, with the logo, to the instant messaging app "Whatsapp". |
| The URL of the Battlestate Games website can be found on a blue panel near the factory shacks. |
| A green screen can be found in one of the buildings with bloodstains, a camera, and a dinosaur toy. It refers to the fictional execution of "Jonathan Miller", a protagonist in the game "Battlefield 3", developed by "DICE". This is also a quest location for the quest Is This a Reference? by Fence. |

sections.heading: Woods
sections.text:
| Description | Screenshot |
| Near the new sawmill, there's a destroyed gate and an exploded car next to it, along with the driver's corpse. This is a reference to the old version of Woods, where this location used to be the border of the map and a vehicle extract. You'll need to visit this location for the Another Shipping Delay quest. | |
| The Old Sawmill is none other than the "Old Sawmill" map from the game Contract Wars, which later appeared in Hired Ops and later Escape from Tarkov: Arena | N/A |
| A wooden bear figure in a burnt-out Zhiguli. Southeast of the flooded village (towards Lihapallo Peak (called Boar's Fang in earlier versions)), under the power lines. This is a reference to the joke "A bear is walking through the forest, sees a burning car, gets in, and burns to death.". This location must be visited for the quest Is This a Reference? | |
| There's a locked room in the BTR base Old house room key, the decor of which mirrors the room featured in the series Escape from Tarkov: The Raid (TV series, 2021). The merchant Ogryzko, who was visited by the series' main character, Skif, sat in this room. | |
| "A piano in the bushes" is a reference to a popular Russian expression. It's located near a large rock west of the Scav Bunker. | |

sections.heading: Shoreline
sections.text:
| Description | Screenshot |
| On a bench near the village, There is a small book with the picture of a dinosaur with the title "All My Friends Are Still Dead". This is a book written by Avery Monsen and Jory John. The same book can be found in the on the second story of the unlocked villa | |
| In a concert room in the health resort you can find an electric guitar modeled on the Fender Stratocaster, with "Bender" printed on the headstock in the style of its real-life counterpart. | N/A |
| Inside one of the compounds there is an upside-down chair on the ceiling. It is believed that this is a reference to the film "The Conjuring". This is also a quest location for the quest Is This a Reference? by Fence. |
| Near the scav watchtower there is a grave with the Russian inscription "Ivan Ivano Ivanovich". "Ivan Ivanovich Ivanov" is the Russian equivalent of naming a person John Smith or John Doe, signifying an unknown person whose name is also unknown. |
| At the North of the map, behind the Resort and near the crashed drone, you can hear a barking dog near the wall. |
| In the ritual spot, a Dead Scav wears severed pig head, this could be considered a reference to the film series "Saw", in which the killer capture his victims by wearing a pig head mask. |
| In the Norvinsk port building, there are two toilets opposite each other in the restroom. This is a reference to the meme of double toilets that gained popularity during the preparations for the 2014 Sochi Olympics. This is also a quest location for the quest Is This a Reference? by Fence. | |
| In a bus, there is a poster with the character "Totoro" that is affixed to the back of the driver cabin. This is a reference to the film "My Neighbor Totoro". | |
| The abandoned sanatorium "Strelna", which is located near St. Petersburg, was a model for the health resort. The building was demolished in 2022. While the building is visibly demolished on Google Maps, it is still intact on Google Street View. | See below |

sections.heading: Hideout
sections.text:
| Description | Screenshot |
| Many elements of the rest space refers to the "Playstation 4", a gaming console produced by Sony.; A blue "TP4" package can be found on top of a shelf in the rest space.; A DualShock 4 controller can be found of the sofa; The console itself can be seen just next to the TV | |
| A "Call of Call" disk case can be found next to the TV when rest space is upgraded to Level 3. This is in reference to the popular FPS game "Call of Duty", produced by Activision Blizzard. | |
| When the Intelligence Center is upgraded to Level 2 it contains a laptop running Kali Linux with the program Armitage having just been opened from the terminal. Kali is a Linux distribution designed for penetration testing and digital forensics, Armitage is a graphical management tool for the Metasploit Framework. | |
| A book called "How to Teach Quantum Physics to Your Dog", written by Chad Orzel, can be found behind the sofa, near the bookcase. | N/A |
| Two other books called "Unity for Dummies and "All my friends are still dead" by Avery Monsen and Jory Johncan can also be found in the bookcase. Unity is the game engine of Escape From Tarkov. |
| The radio on the shelf can be turned on and the song heard is "Wings by geneburn". |

sections.heading: The Lab
sections.text:
- A description from this site about Hamlet from Shakespeare is written on an intravenous infusion.
- The busts on the first level represent four people:
  - Maria Salomea Skłodowska (7 November 1867 – 4 July 1934), also known as Marie Curie, a Polish and naturalized-French physicist and chemist most known for discovering radioactivity.
  - Dmitri Ivanovich Mendeleev (8 February 1834 – 2 February 1907), a Russian chemist and inventor who created the first version of the periodic table of elements.
  - Niels Bohr (7 October 1885 – 18 November 1962), a Danish physicist who worked on atomic structure and quantum theory.
  - Nikolay Nikolaevich Zinin (25 August 1812 – 18 February 1880), a Russian organic chemist who gave his name to the Zinin reaction.
    - In January 2019, a giveaway was held in the official EFT group on the VKontakte social network. The person who was the first to correctly name the names of these scientists received a Secure container Kappa as a gift.

sections.heading: Reserve
sections.text:
- A chess piece with a plug stuck to the bottom can be found in the bottom of one of the bunkers and is related to Resident Evil 2 Classic/Remastered.
- The train station has a graffiti pallet on one of the metal balconies inside which says: "Train hard 715". It is a reference to a channel called "715 TEAM" on Youtube where the main content is military tactics and gear.
- Black bishop building has a graffiti on one of the wall which reads "Fruit_cake малаца!" (roughly translates Fruit_cake good job) apparently for sewer hatch models located across the map which fruit_cake gifted to the developers.
- The underground bunker system is based on "Бункер 703" (Bunker 703) in Moscow, which was in use by the Russian ministry of Foreign Affairs.
- A hole similar to the Batman logo, from the DC Universe, can be found on the white dome on the top of the mountain.

sections.heading: Lighthouse
sections.text:
- Inside of a wardrobe in one of the seaside houses, a motorcycle helmet with goggles can be seen. This may be a reference to the helmet worn by Shinobu Oshino of the Monogatari series.

- Near the northern seaside house, there's a ball with a bloody handprint on it, referencing the movie "Cast Away".

- Not too far away from the "Cast Away" reference, there is an umbrella shaft being stabbed in the middle of a bonfire. This is a reference to the "Dark Souls" games checkpoints.

sections.heading: Streets of Tarkov
sections.text:
- In the room locked with Primorsky 48 apartment key, there is a Doge picture on the shelf in the middle of room.

- View of the building of the LexOs car dealership is based on the building of the Mercedes car dealership in Moscow, at the address Moscow, Leningradsky prospekt, 39a

- Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (TMNT). Near the River exit in the sewer, there are many pizza boxes and skateboards on the sewer floor. Also on the wall, there is an inscription in Russian "Кавабанга" in English it is Cowabunga or Kowabunga - the battle cry of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles.

- A reference to the popular Russian-speaking YouTuber Marmok https://www.youtube.com/@MrMarmok/featured

- Veterinary clinic "Three Paws" (ru: Три лапы) is a reference to the small veterinary clinic "4 Paws" (ru: 4 лапы) located in the city of St. Petersburg.

sections.heading: Ground Zero
sections.text:
- The Nakatani Building is a reference to the film Die Hard (1988), starring Bruce Willis as police officer John McClane. The film takes place in Nakatomi Plaza, which has been taken over by terrorists.
- A reference to a meme of a girl and several African-Americans at a casting for a porn film. Mentioned in the quest Is This a Reference?: The little chair surrounded by big black chairs. In the conference room on the third floor (labeled 5) of the Tarbank building.

sections.heading: Terminal
sections.text:
- One of the shipping containers is a reference to the mission "Hide and Seek" from the game "Ready or Not", where trafficked women can be found in a similar container.

- One of the shipping containers is a reference to the bar "Coyote Ugly Saloon". Inside is a bar with a Russian sign saying "БАР ГАДКИЙ ВАЛЕК", which translates to "Bar Ugly Whitefish".

- A rough replica of the bureau pictured in the short film "PAPERS, PLEASE", based on the game of the same name, including the flag of the fictional nation of Arstotzka can be found.

- A ship is moored near one of the piers, and on the stern is written in Russian, "Головка пальца ноги LATVERIA". In Russian, it's a meaningless phrase. The literal translation is "Toe Head LATVERIA." This is a reference to the film "Fantastic Four" (2005). At the end of the film, this ship was used to transport Doctor Doom, who had been transformed into a statue.

- Graffiti referencing the cover of Nirvana's Nevermind album.

- The Bullet Express logo appears in several places in the Terminal location. It's unclear whether this is a company logo or just graffiti. However, the logo is a reference to the Planet Express company from the animated series Futurama.

sections.heading: Fence
sections.text: - Quest Compensation for Damage - Collection. The final line after the quest says "your request for a new filter for the ProVacuum 60 model," a reference to the TV series Breaking Bad (2008). In the show, there was a store called Best Quality Vacuum. If you went there and said the code phrase "I need a new filter for my Hoover MaxExtract PressurePro model 60 vacuum cleaner," the store owner would help you start your life anew. New documents, a cover story, etc.

sections.heading: Events
sections.text:
- Event Events
  - The event name itself is a reference to the film "Wild Wild West" (1999).
  - The event teaser references "Raiders of the Lost Ark" (1981). If you watch, you can see in the background one Wild West waving a tactical sword and charging at another Wild West, who in turn simply shoots the swordsman.

sections.heading: Scavs
sections.text:
- Scavs sometimes says "А ну чики брики и в дамки!" which phonetically translate to "A nu cheeki breeki I ve damke!". Its meaning is "One, Two, You're on top!". The most known reference is the video game series "S.T.A.L.K.E.R." where the NPCs from Bandits faction said this. But it is also a catchphrase used in chess and nursery universe in Russia.
- Scavs long phrase, “Ублюдок, мать твою, а ну иди сюда...” is a reference to Andrey Gavrilov’s Russian simultaneous translation of the opening scene of the film "Blood and concrete".

sections.heading: USEC
sections.text:
- The voice actor behind the voice called "USEC 3" is the content creator "FortyOne."
- The voice line "Like in the movie: I have a baaaad feeling about this" is a running gag in Star Wars movies.

sections.heading: BEAR
sections.text: - The "Sergei" voice has a small chance to start quietly singing after pressing the key bind for "Mumble."

sections.heading: Therapist
sections.text: - On the 1st of August 2020, the image of Therapist was briefly changed with a Therapist's cosplay by Pestily to celebrate Pestily's goal of 1,000,000$ AUS raised for the Starlight foundation

sections.heading: Killa
sections.text: A cosplay with a more Russian-focused theme of the character "Tachanka", a Spetsnaz operator from the game "Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Siege" that was posted on Reddit, inspired the developers to create Killa. Tachanka is known for his iconic Maska-1SCh helmet.

sections.heading: Weapons variants
sections.text:
- The "Space Trooper" variant of the M4A1 refers to the "Stormtroopers", the soldiers of the "Empire" in the "Star Wars" lore.
- The "Nerfgun" variant of the Saiga-12K references Nerf dart blasters, a popular toy gun series.
- The "CWDG" variant of the FN P90 is the acronym of "Contract Wars DevGru". It refers to the "P90 Devgru" in the game "Contract Wars". It also trade for GP coins.

sections.heading: Melee weapons
sections.text:
- The Freeman crowbar refers to the crowbar wielded by "Gordon Freeman", the main protagonist in the videogame series "Half-Life", by Valve.
- The Red Rebel ice pick is the same as the one used by Lara Croft of the Tomb Raider game series. Both models are based on the discontinued 'Rebel' line of ice tools produced by DMM Wales in the early 2000's.

sections.heading: Weapon mods
sections.text:
- TOZ-106's mosin stock is a joke about "Napiling" which is Russian for filing. It's a half-reference for a famous Russian saying "Dorabotat' napilnikom" which means to modify something so that it works properly.
- The sentence "DA RED GOEZ FASTA" in the description of the AK Hexagon tubular handguard (Anodized Red) is a reference to a faction in Warhammer 40,000, The Orks. Orks believe Red makes things faster, and as all Orks possess some psychic potential in-universe that manifests when they believe strongly enough in something, Red paint provides increased speed to their vehicles.
- The RPK-16 dust cover has "Че тут ищешь?" written underneath, which loosely translates to "What are you looking for here?"

- The FN P90 5.7x28 50-round magazine has "потом будет прозрачный" written on the side, which means "Will be transparent later".
  - After the 1.0 release, the words were replaced with "Походу не будет :(" instead, which translates as "Looks like it won't happen :("

- The yellow banana version of the AK 7.62x39 Magpul PMAG 30 GEN M3 30-round magazine has a QR code on the side that reads "Тебе делать совсем нехуй ?", roughly translates to "Do you seriously have nothing fucking better to do?"

- SR-3M Karden rail handguard is based on the work of Karden, a Russian blogger and member of a special forces unit. The process and development of how the handguard came about can be read here.

sections.heading: Chest rigs
sections.text: - The Crye Precision CPC plate carrier (Goons Edition) features a mirrored iPhone 7 Plus in a Magpul MAG849-ORG field case.

sections.heading: Face cover
sections.text:
- The Slender mask is a reference to the faceless monster "Slenderman" of the creepypasta "The Slenderman".
- The Misha Mayorov mask refers to "Michael Myers" the anti hero in the film "Halloween".
- The Jason mask is the same as the mask wear by "Jason Voorhees" in the film "Friday the 13th".
- The Ghost balaclava is a reference to the balaclava worn by Simon "Ghost" Riley in the video game Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2.
- The Faceless mask is a reference to the character "No-Face" featured in the animated film "Spirited Away".
- The Hockey player mask (Quiet), Hockey player mask (Captain), Hockey player mask (Brawler) is a reference to the Soviet cartoon "Puck! Puck!" (1964)
- The Atomic Defense CQCM ballistic mask (Stop Me) is directly inspired by a mask featured in the game "Manhunt", worn by members of the gang "The Smileys", which are named after their off-putting smiley masks.

sections.heading: Headwear
sections.text:
- The Santa hat and Fake white beard refer to the Santa Claus or Saint Nicholas. This is a legendary figure, originating in Western Christian culture, who is said to bring gifts to the homes of well-behaved children on Christmas Eve.
- The Ded Moroz hat refers to a fictional character by the same name who brings presents to well-mannered children on New Year's Eve
- The Door Kicker boonie hat refers to the strategy game "Door Kickers", developed by KillHouse Games and also to the game Character "Captain Price" from the CoD Modern Warfare series in which Price wears the same hat.
- The Tac-Kek Heavy Trooper mask for Ops-Core-type helmets refer to the helmet of "Heavy Trooper", a "Clone" type in the "Star Wars" lore. The description has a quote from the show "The Mandalorian" which is set in the same universe.
- The Baseball cap feature the logo of Superman, the superhero from DC Universe.
- The Bomber beanie refers to Edd's beanie from the cartoon show "Ed,Edd, n Eddy".

sections.heading: Eyewear
sections.text: - The RayBench Hipster Reserve sunglasses and RayBench Aviator glasses are parodies of the sunglasses brand Ray Ban

sections.heading: Tactical Clothing
sections.text:
- The USEC Aggressor TAC jacket is modeled on the Aggressor Parka™ and the gloves after the TAC K9 and Rope Handler Glove both made by 5.11 Tactical.
- The USEC Softshell Flexion jacket is modeled on the Blackhawk Waterproof Jacket, and gloves are modeled on the Oakley Flexion Gloves.
- The USEC Taclife Terrain pants are modeled on the Blackhawk Tac Life Pant, and the boots are modeled on the Ariat Terrain Boot.
- The USEC Gen.2 Khyber pants are modeled on the Kitanica Gen2 Pants, and the boots are modeled on the Khyber Lightweight Tactical Boot.
- The USEC PCU Ironsight jacket is modeled on the ORC Industries PCU Level 5 jacket, and gloves are modeled on the Outdoor Research Ironsight gloves.
- The USEC PCS MultiCam shirt is modeled on the British Army PCS Combat Shirt, and gloves are modeled on the Mechanix M-Pact MultiCam gloves.
- The USEC Woodland Infiltrator upper shirt is modeled on the TRU-SPEC T.R.U. 1/4 Zip Combat Shirt, and gloves are modeled on the Mechanix The Original gloves.
- The USEC Commando sweater is modeled on the Rothco USMC Commando Sweater and gloves are modeled on the First Tactical Pro Knuckle Glove.
- The USEC Standard upper shirt is modeled on the Crye Precision G3 Combat Shirt and gloves are modeled on the Oakley SI Assault Gloves.
- The USEC Night Patrol jacket is modeled after the MOS Tactical Gen 2 Night Camo Parka and the gloves are modeled after the Magpul Patrol Glove 2.0.
- The USEC Woodland Infiltrator lower pants are modeled on the Crye Precision G3 Combat Pants in Woodland camouflage.
- The USEC TACRES pants are modeled on the TRU-SPEC T.R.U. Pants.
- The USEC Deep Recon pants are modeled on the Helikon-Tex UTP Pants, and the boots are modeled on the Lowa Zephyr TF series.
- The USEC Legionnaire lower The pants are modeled on the Clawgear Raider (MKIV) Series Combat Pants. The model also uses the older D3O Clawgear Trust HP knee pads.
- The BEAR Standard lower pants are modeled on SRVV REITER, the pistol holster is modeled on the ANA Tactical Universal MOLLE Holster, and the knife and sheath are modeled on the Kizlyar Supreme Feldjaeger.
- The BEAR Zaslon lower pants are modeled on the Kitanica All Season Pants, and the boots are modeled on the Lowa Zephyr GTX Hi TF.
- The BEAR Zaslon upper shirt is modeled on the SSO RAID summer suit, and gloves are modeled on the Blackhawk F.U.R.Y. Utilitarian gloves.
- The BEAR Summer Field upper jacket is modeled on the SSO FIELD 5 N summer suit, and gloves are modeled on the Outdoor Research Halberd Sensor Gloves.
- The BEAR Summer Field lower pants are modeled on the SSO FIELD 5 N summer suit.
- The BEAR Black Lynx jacket is modeled on the SSO Lynx fleece jacket, and gloves are modeled on the Oakley Factory Lite Tactical gloves.
- The BEAR Ghost Marksman jacket is modeled on the Sniper mantle "Ghost" and the "SSO GORKA-E", and gloves are modeled on the 5.11 Tactical Scene One Gloves.
- The BEAR Telnik shirt is modeled on the dark blue stripe Telnyashka worn by the Russian Marines.
- The BEAR G99 lower pants are modeled on the Gruppa 99 L10 Tropical Combat Pants and the holster is modeled on the SSO KO 3 hip holster.
- The BEAR G99 upper shirt is modeled on the Gruppa 99 L10 Tropical Combat Shirt, and gloves are modeled on the Viktos LEO Vented Duty Glove.
- The BEAR Oldschool pants are modeled on the Soviet Union TTsKO camouflage summer trousers, and the shoes are modeled on either Nike, Puma or Mockba brand sneakers of the 1980’s.
- The BEAR VOLK gloves are modeled after Wiley-X DURTAC SmartTouch Gloves.

sections.heading: Secure containers
sections.text:
- The Secure container Alpha is modeled after the iM2050 Storm Case by Pelican. The only differences between the real life counterpart and the in-game model is the handle type.
- The Secure container Gamma is modeled after the SE Series™ Scoped Pistol Case by Plano. The only differences between the real life counterpart and the in-game model is coloration.
- The Secure container Kappa is modeled after the V100 by Pelican. As with the Secure container Gamma, the only differences between the real life counterpart and the in-game model is coloration.

sections.heading: Barter Items
sections.text:
- The Bottle of Tarkovskaya vodka description refers to the "Storm Area 51" meme.
- The Xenomorph sealing foam is a reference to the "Xenomorph" which is the monster in the horror film series "Alien".
- The Slickers Bar has humorous writing throughout the ingredients list written on the side.

- The Chain with Prokill medallion refers to the killstreak "Prokill" in the prequels of EFT, "Contract Wars" and "Hired Ops".
- The GP coin is a reference to one of BSG's previous games "Contract Wars" in which GP was the premium currency.
- The Graphics card is modeled after an ASUS GeForce GTX 750 Ti GPU.

- The LEDX Skin Transilluminator is based directly on the Veinlite LEDX Vein Finder.

- The SSD drive is modeled after a SSD Samsung EVO 840 250 GB SSD.
- The SAS drive is modeled after a ICYDOCK ToughArmor MB991IK-B Rugged 2.5" SAS/SATA HDD & SSD Mobile Rack.
- The Portable Powerbank is based off Xiaomi's "Mi Power Bank 10400mAh" model.
- The Portable defibrillator is based off Philips HeartStart FRx Automated external defibrillator.
- The Military flash drive is based off TECHAYA MILTECH M64 MIL-STD flash drive.
